record.paper_title: Braking index of isolated pulsars: open questions and ways forward
record.context_brief: Mismatch between observed and canonical pulsar braking indices
record.original_question: What physical spin-down model can explain isolated pulsars whose braking index, defined observationally from angular velocity Ω and its first and second time derivatives as n = ΩΩ̈/Ω̇², is measured in the range about 1 < n < 2.8, even though the standard magnetic-dipole-radiation model predicts n = 3 and the canonical particle-wind, magnetic-dipole-radiation, and quadrupole-radiation torque mechanisms predict n = 1, 3, and 5 respectively?

evidence.quote: The MDR model predicts n exactly equal to 3. Selected observations of isolated pulsars provide rather precise values of n, individually accurate to a few percent or better, in the range 1 < n < 2.8, which is consistently less than the predictions of the MDR model. In spite of an extensive investigation of various modiﬁcations of the MDR model, no satisfactory explanation of observation has been found as of yet.
For each mechanism described above, the t heoretical braking index is n = 1, 3, 5 for particle wind, MDR, and quadrupole radiation respectively.
It is clear that none of these observed stars has a bra king index consistent with any of the values produced from theory.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For an isolated rotating neutron star (pulsar) with angular velocity Ω(t), define the observational braking index by

  n = Ω Ω̈ / (Ω̇)²,

equivalently obtained from a spin-down law Ω̇ = −K Ω^n with K constant. The standard canonical torque mechanisms predict the following discrete values: n = 1 for a pure relativistic particle wind, n = 3 for pure magnetic dipole radiation in vacuum (the MDR model), and n = 5 for pure magnetic quadrupole radiation. Observationally, however, several isolated pulsars have measured braking indices, accurate to within a few percent or better, lying strictly between these predictions, in the approximate range 1 < n < 2.8.

Problem: Construct a physical spin-down model for an isolated pulsar — specifying the torque(s), magnetospheric configuration, and any time evolution of relevant quantities (such as magnetic field strength, magnetic inclination angle, moment of inertia, or particle outflow) — that yields, in a self-consistent way, braking indices continuously taking values in the observed range 1 < n < 2.8, and that quantitatively reproduces the precisely measured n values of the known isolated pulsars without requiring fine-tuning beyond what is astrophysically justified.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature continues to propose modifications to the magnetic-dipole-radiation model — including combined particle wind plus dipole torques, time-varying inclination angle or magnetic field, magnetospheric reconnection, and effective-force corrections — to account for braking indices in the range 1 < n < 3, but no single model has been broadly accepted as quantitatively reproducing all measured values. The problem is generally treated as still open.

status_evidence.title: Braking Index of Isolated Pulsars
status_evidence.snippet: Discusses ongoing efforts to explain measured braking indices below 3 for isolated pulsars.
status_evidence.claim: The discrepancy between measured indices and the MDR prediction remains an active research topic.

status_evidence.title: Braking indices of pulsars obtained in the presence of an effective force
status_evidence.snippet: Proposes an effective-force modification yielding braking indices less than 3.
status_evidence.claim: New phenomenological models continue to be proposed to fit observed n values.

status_evidence.title: Magnetic field growth in young glitching pulsars with a braking index
status_evidence.snippet: Models time-varying magnetic field as a mechanism producing n < 3.
status_evidence.claim: No single accepted explanation; multiple competing models exist.
